phases.message: I'm worried we're letting changes slide on Westfold. Start here in Primeline GC: read the subcontract terms on claims, changes, markup and scope, and what's already been made a change order or noticed.
Now Sitegrid: every RFI, ASI and directive that touches our work, and what each one actually tells us to do.
This is Dailylog. Read the foremen's entries since mid-September for anything that changed our work, and when.
Now Estimato. Get the cost of every PCO, and any lower-tier sub in it.
Back in Primeline GC. Give notice on every change we're still entitled to claim, priced with the markup and dated right. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

terms.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Primeline GC, subcontractor portal for the Westfold Medical Office Building. Subcontract PL-2291 with Corvane Electric LLC. Topics: contract, claims, changes, markup, scope. Give one notice per change event (Corvane's PCO number); a notice given here is written notice under the subcontract.

Subcontract PL-2291 incorporates by reference AIA Document A201-2017, General Conditions of the Contract for Construction, as it forms part of the prime contract between Westfold Health Partners and Primeline Builders. Corvane is bound to Primeline as Primeline is bound to the owner. A201-2017 is a published standard form; the clauses this portal relies on are summarized here in Primeline's words, not quoted.

The notice window (A201-2017 section 15.1.3.1, summarized, applied by Subcontract section 11.2): a claim for more money or time is started by written notice within 21 days after the event that gives rise to it, or within 21 days after Corvane first recognizes the condition that gives rise to it, whichever is later. Days are calendar days. For a change directed by an RFI answer, an ASI, a field directive or a CCD, the event is the day of the direction. A concealed or unknown condition (section 3.7.4, summarized) is noticed within 14 days after Corvane first observes that it differs from the documents. A claim not noticed inside its window is waived (Subcontract section 11.3).

Changes (A201-2017 Article 7, summarized): the Work is changed by change order, by construction change directive (CCD), or by the architect's order for a minor change. A CCD directs the work now and leaves the price to be agreed: answer it with a notice and your price. Work the contract documents already show or specify is not a change, and an RFI answer that confirms the documents ('as shown') changes nothing. Rework of Corvane's own non-conforming work, and delay Corvane caused, are Corvane's cost. The subcontract price is fixed, with no escalation clause: a rise in material prices is not a change. An event already made a change order, or already noticed, is not noticed again.

Price a notice at Corvane's cost from its estimate plus markup (Subcontract section 11.5): 15% on Corvane's own labor and material (10% overhead and 5% profit, each on cost), and 5% on a lower-tier subcontractor's cost. Enter the total in dollars to the cent, and the date of the event or of recognition.

Exhibit A, Corvane's scope: Divisions 26 (electrical), 27 (communications) and 28 (fire detection and alarm: devices, wiring and panel) complete, per the drawings and specifications. Excluded: temporary power and temporary lighting, which are Primeline's under section 01 50 00.

change_orders.subject: Lobby pendants changed from type L2 to type L4 (ASI-11)

items.subject: Nurses' station data drops
items.text: Add four data drops at the nurses' station, room 140, cabled per section 27 15 00.

items.subject: Lobby pendants
items.text: Lobby pendants change from type L2 to type L4. Price and submit.

items.subject: Corridor fire alarm layout
items.text: Corridor fire alarm devices are relocated to match the revised ceiling grid. No devices are added; the fire alarm remains as specified in section 28 31 00.

items.subject: Panel LP-2 location
items.text: Asked 21 Sept by Corvane: panel LP-2, installed in corridor 1B where E-101 locates it, blocks the access to the fire damper the mechanical drawings put beside it. Answered 24 Sept by the architect: relocate LP-2 to electrical room 112 per sketch SK-E-07, and extend the feeders as required.

items.subject: Break-room receptacles
items.text: Asked 17 Sept by Corvane: the city plan reviewer's comment 14 asks for GFCI protection in the break rooms; E-301 shows standard receptacles. Answered 19 Sept by the architect: provide GFCI protection at every break-room receptacle, rooms 118 and 214.

items.subject: Reception desk receptacle
items.text: Asked 21 Sept by Corvane: is the reception desk receptacle wall-mounted or in a floor box? Answered 23 Sept by the architect: provide as shown on E-401, detail 5 (floor box). No change to the contract documents.

items.subject: Exam rooms 4 to 6 receptacles
items.text: Add six duplex receptacles and one dedicated 20 A circuit in exam rooms 4 to 6 for the owner's new equipment.

items.subject: Exam-room lighting controls
items.text: Exam-room lighting controls change to dual-level occupancy sensors.

items.subject: Second transfer switch, imaging suite
items.text: Signed by the owner, the architect and Primeline: provide feeders, conduit and controls wiring for a second automatic transfer switch (ATS-2) serving the imaging suite. Proceed now; the price is to be agreed under the change provisions. Answer with your cost and markup.

logs.note: Opened the ceiling in corridor B of the existing wing. Old conduit and cable above it, which the existing-conditions drawing ED-101 shows as abandoned. Left in place, as ED-101 says.
Crew of four stood by 16 and 17 Sept: Primeline's drywall crew had not closed the corridor C ceiling, so our rough-in there could not go on. Told Primeline's superintendent.
RFI-60 answered: GFCI protection in both break rooms. Devices ordered.
Our crew ran conduit in corridor D at 9'-0"; E-201 shows 10'-6". Pulling it and re-running it, two days, our cost.
RFI-58 answered: LP-2 moves to room 112. Core drilling booked with Truecore Cutting.

Meter-tested the old circuits above corridor B: three are live and feed the pharmacy's refrigerators, though ED-101 shows them abandoned. Westfold facilities (K. Abernathy) confirmed. They must be re-fed from LP-3 before the corridor ceiling work goes on.
Notice NC-12 sent to Primeline for the ASI-13 lighting controls.
Primeline's superintendent, D. Rourke, told us on site to run temporary power to the trailer compound, two 100 A services. Done 1 and 2 Oct.
City rough-in inspection failed: our panel directories were not labeled. Re-inspection booked for 6 Oct; half a day of standby.
Supplier letter: copper building wire is up 14% since our bid in March.
CCD-03 rough-in started. Halden Power Services booked for the ATS-2 startup and testing.
Exam rooms 4 to 6 receptacles (ASI-14) roughed in.
